messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
Here's the post. I used a placeholder app name — swap `Marginal` for your own.

---

# Dark mode, finally

Dark mode ships today in Marginal 3.2. Settings → Appearance, or set it to follow your system.

This took longer than it should have. Our first build was a straight inversion of the light palette, and it was awful — pure white text on pure black, which makes a long paragraph shimmer after about two minutes of reading. So we pulled in both ends. Body text now sits at #E4E4E7 on a #18181B background, roughly a 13:1 contrast ratio instead of 21:1.

Everything layered on top had to be re-tuned. The yellow highlighter went warmer and dropped in saturation, because the original burned a hole through the page. Code blocks got their own syntax theme rather than the light one with the background swapped. Link blue was unreadable at 40% opacity in the sidebar, so links there are now underlined instead of tinted.

Two things people kept asking for, both in:

- **Scheduled switching.** Sunset to sunrise by default, or pick your own hours.
- **Per-note override.** Keep a single note light while the rest of the app stays dark. Useful if you paste in screenshots.

Images and PDFs are untouched. We tried dimming them automatically and it made everyone's scanned receipts look moldy.

If something reads wrong — a color that vibrates, a border that disappears — tell us at support@marginal.app and include a screenshot. We fixed eleven of these during beta and we expect more.

Update from the App Store, or it'll arrive on its own within a day.
